insights.summary: Q1 FY27 revenue was ₹141.6 Cr (down 10% YoY) with operational EBITDA margin of 27.3% and PAT of ₹34.5 Cr, including a ₹3.4 Cr fire loss. New orders were only ₹44.6 Cr, so the order book fell to ₹1,239 Cr; a ₹177.5 Cr Ministry of Defence simulator order came after the quarter. Management expects revenue to pick up in Q2-Q3, a mid-30s EBITDA margin for FY27 and a ₹2,500 Cr order book by March 2027, but blames a lack of government tenders for slow orders.

what_changed.text: Order book target of about ₹2,500 Cr at the end of FY27
Full-year operational EBITDA margin in the mid-30s despite 27.3% in Q1
₹177.5 Cr MoD order to upgrade and integrate tank and crew gunnery simulators
Big simulator orders (₹700-800 Cr) still expected 'soon'; one may take a couple of months

tone.label: cautious
tone.quote: What I have learned from frequent prediction is not to make any prediction.

analyst_questions.answer: Fixed costs on lower revenue; Q1 FY26 had ₹7.65 Cr of provision releases; gross margin steady at 72.9%.
MD: a demand problem, no anti-drone or simulator tenders floated recently; fast-track tenders expected.
About ₹2,500 Cr after this year's execution, as pipeline converts.
Working through compliance (FOCI, ITAR) and partnering primes; modest aim of $100 million in year three.

red_flags.text: Only ₹44.6 Cr of orders in Q1; order book fell to ₹1,239 Cr, far from what ₹4,000 Cr of revenue in two years needs.
Orders promised for Q1 did not arrive; MD says no tenders have been floated.
Working capital rose to 257 days on supplier advances and inventory.
Q1 EBITDA margin 27.3% vs 35% guided; one-off fire loss of ₹3.4 Cr.
